title: Trump signs law as India risks 100% tariffs over Russian oil
content:
US President Donald Trump has signed H.R. 5334, expanding sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extending existing sanctions on Iran. 
The law can expose goods from top Russian oil and gas buyers, including India and China, to duties of up to 100 per cent. 
Importers and sourcing teams face possible tariff changes within 30 days of signing.

title: India's FY27 GDP forecast raised to 7% on economic resilience: Moody’s
content:
Moody’s Ratings has raised its forecast for India’s real GDP growth in FY2026-27 to 7 per cent from 6 per cent, citing stronger-than-expected economic momentum and resilience to global disruptions. 
Growth is being supported by private consumption, infrastructure investment and sustained services activity. 
Moody’s maintained a stable outlook on India’s Baa3 sovereign rating.

title: India’s trade gains face new tariff uncertainty
content:
New Zealand’s Parliament has passed legislation to implement the India FTA, with all Indian goods to receive duty-free access after ratification.
For Indian textiles, apparel and made-ups, removing 5-10 per cent duties could improve price competitiveness in New Zealand.
A US sanctions bill could allow tariffs of up to 100 per cent on Russian energy buyers, adding risk to India-US trade talks.

title: Weak demand drags cotton yarn prices lower in South India
content:
Cotton yarn prices declined in Tiruppur and Mumbai as weak downstream demand, payment constraints and falling cotton prices kept buyers cautious.
Tiruppur prices dipped ₹4-5 per kg, while Mumbai eased ₹3-5 per kg amid slow local demand and reduced fabric production.
Gujarat cotton prices fell with ICE futures; mills avoided stocks ahead of new-crop arrivals, which scanty rains may delay.

title: US cotton exports weaken as Upland shipments fall 20%
content:
US Upland cotton net sales for 2026-27 fell 4 per cent to 71,200 RB, 30 per cent below the four-week average; Vietnam led buying.
Upland shipments dropped 20 per cent to 142,100 RB, while Pima sales fell 17 per cent to 8,300 RB but stayed above average.
Pima shipments declined 22 per cent to 4,100 RB, with India leading; weak exports pressured ICE cotton futures as US harvest advanced.
